issue: Dark striped grass bank at native5550–5770 m. Prior mesh analysis found front-facing, unoccluded terrain with low sun incidence. The former negative interpolated-normal claim was withdrawn.
finding: Spa Grass inherits NormalStrength0.18 from the Interlagos material instance. Its parent normalizes (Normal.xy*Strength, lerp(1,Normal.z,Strength)). On steep slopes at low light incidence this micro-normal map may produce dark bands. This is a shading hypothesis to test, not a demonstrated terrain defect.
status: Normal-strength candidate failed and is reverted in source. Daylight orientation candidate is source-only until rebuilt, packaged and checked around the whole route. No visual fix is claimed.

normal_strength_test.result: Rejected. The bank remains dark in the station-matched whole-lap review. Material inspection records DefaultNormal, so varying strength does not alter a flat tangent normal. Restore0.18.

daylight_candidate.rationale: Spa-only authored afternoon light direction illuminates the source-grounded bank. Same sunlight elevation, energy, sky intensity, exposure, shadows, terrain, normals and camera. The sun azimuth/elevation is physically possible at Spa latitude; no exact event time is claimed. Sky cubemap and visible dome rotate with the sun, following existing venue-specific daylight conventions.
